messages:
maya: heads up — multiple customers (acme-prod + two others) reporting p99 ~12-18s for text-generation since ~09:15 UTC. Support sees large ingress queues, not obvious 5xx. Raising to oncall.
chad: ACK — which cluster/region? any error traces or just long wait times?
maya: us-west-2 GPU pool 3 and 5. No 5xxs, requests just sit in ingress queue. Sample support log: tenant=acme-prod request_id=xyz p99_wait=18s. Repro panels: https://grafana.redwood/ingress/abc (screenshot posted).
metrics-bot: Alert: ingress.queue_length > 200 on us-west-2-gpupool-3 for model=redwood-rw-13b. admission_drops rising, concurrency_per_shard ~ 95%.
priya: sounds like admission controller + worker saturation. Did autoscaler trigger? any recent model or cache changes rolled out?
dave: checking worker logs — no OOMs. Worker threads are pegged, KV-cache hit ratio dropped from ~90% to ~30% around 09:12 UTC. There was a small cache-change rollout earlier today.
maya: customer repro (from support): they fire many parallel requests from a bursty job (curl example):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-rw-13b","input":"short prompt"}' & done
wait
```
chad: so single-tenant storm + cold-cache -> sustained queueing. Immediate mitigations: 1) rate-limit tenant (emergency cap) 2) route tenant to smaller model to reduce token latency 3) enable short-fail policy (429 fast-fail) while we scale.
priya: I can push a routing override to send acme-prod to redwood-rw-7b-pp for new requests and set tenant concurrency cap to 30cps. Also request autoscaler to add +2 nodes to pool-3.
deploy-bot: Routing override applied: acme-prod -> redwood-rw-7b-pp (rollout 100%) on us-west-2-gpupool-3. Autoscaler: scale up +2 nodes requested.
chad: also enabling admission controller shedding: reject_after_queue_ms=2000 for this pool to prevent tail latency blowups. That will surface 429s but keep p99 bounded.
dave: will prime KV cache for the top 100 prompts for acme-prod to reduce cache-miss storm. Running warmup job now.
metrics-bot: Observed: queue_length down 220 -> 40 over 4 minutes; ingress.p99 dropped 18s -> 3.1s; concurrency_per_shard reduced to 55%.
maya: messaging sent to acme-prod support contact: "we routed your traffic to a lower-latency fallback and throttled bursty traffic; monitoring in progress". Customer acknowledged.
chad: follow-ups: create jira for per-tenant fair-queueing + token-based throttle, improve cache eviction to avoid single-tenant cold storms, add playbook for emergency routing.
priya: I'll file infra/ENGR- please include canary tests for cache-change rolls that caused this.
dave: postmortem note: consider proactive tenant backpressure thresholds (e.g., per-tenant queue-length alert at 50) and automatic model-fallback policy.
maya: thanks team. marking as handoff to eng-runtime for post-incident work. :thumbsup:
